instrument_name: Louisiana Withholding Tables and Formulas R-1306 (1/26)
article_or_section: Computer formula method; Examples 1-2; wage bracket tables (21 pp.)
figure_or_rule_carried: Effective on or after 2026-01-01. Flat 3.09% withholding rate; 2026 standard deduction 12,875 (single / married separate, L-4 '1') and 25,750 (MFJ, QSS, HoH, L-4 '2'); W=S*0.0309 (no deduction), W=(S-(12,875/N))*0.0309, W=(S-(25,750/N))*0.0309; N = 365/52/26/24/12/1; negative variable = zero. Example 1: 700 weekly, '1' -> 13.98; Example 2: 4,600 biweekly, '2' -> 111.54 (oracle seed). Certificate Form R-1300 (L-4). Tables in dollars and cents. Local copy supplies the file missing from US-LA-PIT-001.

instrument_name: Louisiana Register Vol. 52 No. 3 (2026-03-20), Rule 2603#037: Mobile Workforce Exemption (LAC 61:I.1923), adopted
authority: Louisiana Department of Revenue, Tax Policy and Planning Division (published in the Louisiana Register)
article_or_section: LAC 61:I.1923 A.2.a, A.2.d (repealed), C.1.a, C.1.b.i, C.2; LR 52:358
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: ADOPTED - final Rule published LR 52:358 (March 2026), 'adopted on the day of promulgation' (2026-03-20); implements Act 382 of 2025 (R.S. 47:112.2, 47:248(B)(1)(a)). LEVEL: withholding + employer reporting + nonresident return. A.2.a: exemption for compensation for duties performed in LA by a nonresident for 30 or fewer days in the calendar year; A.2.d (home-State / federal-rules condition) repealed. C.1.a: exempt nonresident files no LA return; if the nonresident has other LA-source income the exemption does not apply. C.1.b.i: employee notifies employer within 10 days from the 31st day. C.2: employer begins withholding and reports on Form L-1 beginning in the period in which the 31st day fell. Text inconsistency: C.1.a says 'less than 30 days' while A.2.a and the statute say '30 or fewer'; statute governs. Rendered and read page images (text layer empty).

instrument_name: Louisiana Department of Revenue - Withholding page (Wayback snapshot 2026-10-04 of page updated 2026-06-30)
article_or_section: Electronic Filing and Payment Required; Who Must File; Payment Frequency; Annual Reconciliation; Amended Return; Closing
figure_or_rule_carried: Returns and payments must be filed and paid electronically (LaTAP or approved software). Quarterly return Form L-1 for every assigned period, zero returns required. Payment frequency by average monthly withholding: quarterly < 500; monthly 500 to < 5,000; semi-monthly >= 5,000. Annual reconciliation Form L-3 filed electronically (LaWage) due January 31 following the year, or 30 days after final wages if the business closes. Amended L-1 per quarter, by month. Stopping filings does not close the account. Same page as US-LA-P5-1-001; this row carries the reporting figures.

instrument_name: La. R.S. 23:633 (paydays; notice of wages, method and frequency), 23:634 (forfeiture contracts), 23:635 (fines and deductions)
figure_or_rule_carried: 23:633(A): employer must inform employees at hire of wage rate, method and frequency of payment and any change; employer that fails to designate paydays pays on the 1st and 16th. (B) manufacturing, oil boring and mining with 10+ employees and public service corporations pay at least twice monthly, paydays about two weeks apart, wages due no later than the payday ending the next payroll period (clerical/salesmen excluded except public service corps). (C) excludes FLSA-exempt / executive, administrative, supervisory, professional. (D) LWC notice posting. (E) fine 25-250 USD per day. 23:634(B): pre-employment medical/drug-test cost may be withheld if employee resigns within 90 working days, only if paid >= federal minimum + 1 USD and not part-time/seasonal. 23:635: no fines or deductions as fines except wilful/negligent damage or theft conviction, limited to actual damage. 23:633 history line in the 2026-03-07 snapshot ends at Acts 2014 No. 417 (no 2025 amendment codified).

instrument_name: La. R.S. 23:642 Setting minimum wage or employee benefits; prohibited (local preemption)
figure_or_rule_carried: No local governmental subdivision may establish a minimum wage rate or a mandatory minimum number of vacation or sick leave days (paid or unpaid) for private employers. So no parish/city minimum wage or local paid sick leave in LA. Wayback snapshot 2026-10-24.

instrument_name: Louisiana Workforce Commission - Employer UI tax FAQ (Wayback snapshot 2025-04-22)
article_or_section: Due dates; filing method; part-time employees; tax rate

instrument_name: LAC 61:I.1515 Withholding Tax Statements and Returns - Electronic Filing Requirements; and adjoining LAC 61:I.1501 due dates (Louisiana Administrative Code, March 2022 edition, LDR copy)
authority: Louisiana Department of Revenue (Louisiana Administrative Code)
article_or_section: LAC 61:I.1515 A-E; W-2 paper format 4.a-c; LAC 61:I.1501 A (quarterly due dates)
figure_or_rule_carried: L-1 filed electronically quarterly (periods after 2011-12-31). Form L-3 transmittal + W-2s due on or before the first business day following January 31 (business terminating: within 30 days after the last month wages paid); weekend/holiday -> next business day. Employers filing 50 or more W-2s (due on/after 2016-01-01) must file L-3, W-2s and information returns electronically; options: LaWage on the LDR website or another method authorized by the secretary; magnetic tape, CD and DVD no longer allowed; separate submission per employer. State W-2 core boxes 16-18. Quarterly remittance due Apr 30 / Jul 31 / Oct 31 / Jan 31, with monthly and semi-monthly exceptions by amount withheld. Historical note LR 44:1638 (Sept 2018) is the latest amendment printed.

instrument_name: LDR FAQ: Are employers required to file Form L-3 and the employees' W-2 forms electronically? (Wayback 2026-01-06)
figure_or_rule_carried: Yes: an employer required to file 50 or more W-2s must file all information returns electronically; W-2G electronically when gaming withholding applies (LAC 61:I.1525); penalty for failure to e-file.

instrument_name: La. R.S. 46:236.14 Employer reporting program (state directory of new hires)
figure_or_rule_carried: Report to DCFS (child support enforcement section) the hire of anyone expected to be paid and every rehire/return to work after layoff, furlough, separation, leave without pay or termination; no later than 20 days after hire or rehire; electronic/magnetic filers send two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart; multistate employers may designate one state (written notice to DCFS). Content: employee name, address, SSN, occupation, date services first performed; employer name, address, EIN. On a W-4 or equivalent form, by mail or electronically. Penalty up to 25 USD per failure; up to 500 USD if conspiracy. Wayback snapshot 2025-04-21.

instrument_name: LDR Revenue Information Bulletin No. 26-005 Notice Concerning Updated Withholding Tables Effective January 2026
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: emergency rule (LAC 61:I.1501) effective 2026-01-01 updating withholding tables (in force; final-rule adoption not checked). LEVEL: withholding. Withholding tables use standard deduction 12,875 (single/MFS) and 25,750 (MFJ/QSS/HoH), computed on CPI-U data available at 2025-12-01; official 2026 standard deduction may differ slightly once January 2026 CPI-U is applied. Standard deduction indexed annually by CPI-U increase of the previous year, R.S. 47:294(B). Employees review Form R-1300 (L-4). RIB is informal, not binding.

instrument_name: La. R.S. 13:3881 General exemptions from seizure (wage garnishment exemption)
figure_or_rule_carried: Exempt: 75% of weekly disposable earnings, never less than 30 x federal minimum hourly wage (pro-rated for other pay periods) -> same as CCPA for ordinary creditors. Support: exemption 50% of disposable earnings for child support (current or past due) and 60% for spousal support; mixed or unclear child+spouse orders enforced by DCFS treated as child support. So LA caps child-support garnishment at 50% (stricter than CCPA 50-65%). Disposable earnings = after legally required withholdings and reasonable usual-course deductions for retirement, medical and life insurance and amounts owed to employer. Wayback snapshot 2026-04-10; last amendment Acts 2020 No. 44.

instrument_name: La. R.S. 23:965 Jury duty; dismissal forbidden; uninterrupted compensation; penalties
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee regularly employed in LA called to a state petit or grand jury or central jury pool gets leave of up to ONE day for jury duty without loss of wages or of sick, emergency or personal leave or other benefit (paid jury day). No discharge/adverse action for jury service if employee gives notice. Penalties: reinstatement + fine 100-1,000 USD per discharged employee; fine 100-500 USD for failing to pay the day. Wayback snapshot 2026-09-23; history ends Acts 2003 No. 678 (effective date shown is the Acts 2003 general effective date, not verified).

instrument_name: La. R.S. 23:640 Fringe benefits payable under collective bargaining agreements
figure_or_rule_carried: Amounts payable by employers under CBAs for vacation, health and welfare, pension, apprenticeship/training, supplemental unemployment or other fringe benefits are treated as wages due under R.S. 23:631-639 (same penalties and enforcement as ordinary wages).
